data.title: Light through the old slides

memoryNodes.cue: The projector shines light through a piece of film.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 投影仪让光穿过一片胶片。

memoryNodes.cue: The class checks claims against evidence.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 课堂把说法与证据对照。

memoryNodes.cue: Lin limits her assignment to one question.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 林把作业限制在一个问题上。

data.situation:
For the next class, a lecturer brought a box of old slides from the street archive. Each small piece of photographic film was held in a frame. She placed one in a projector, and light carried its image onto the wall. Lin could see a market stall where the bakery now stood. The lecturer asked the class to draw on these pictures as well as the written records. Questions for the archive visit
What can this photograph tell us?
What would we need to check in another source?
Critical thinking means examining claims and the evidence behind them. Use logical thinking to connect a claim, a reason and a conclusion. A confident caption is still a claim we can question. Lin: I have the skeleton of an essay, but not a complete argument yet.
Tutor: Show me the main points. This is a short assignment, not a dissertation. You don't have to tell the whole history of the town.
Lin: I'd like to acquire a better knowledge of the street first.
Tutor: The acquisition of knowledge takes time. Start with the question on your first page. Lin took a critical look at her own first paragraph. It said the market had always been busy, but one photograph could not show every year. She crossed out always and added the date from the caption. The outline on her desk was small enough to finish. The light on the wall still showed the old bread stall.

readingBlocks.en: For the next class, a lecturer brought a box of old slides from the street archive. Each small piece of photographic film was held in a frame. She placed one in a projector, and light carried its image onto the wall. Lin could see a market stall where the bakery now stood. The lecturer asked the class to draw on these pictures as well as the written records.
readingBlocks.zh: 下一堂课，讲师带来一盒街道档案中的旧幻灯片。每一小片摄影胶片都固定在框里。她把一片放进投影仪，光将图像投到墙上。林看见，现在面包店所在的地方曾有一个集市摊位。讲师让大家利用这些图片，也利用文字记录。

readingBlocks.en:
Questions for the archive visit
What can this photograph tell us?
What would we need to check in another source?
Critical thinking means examining claims and the evidence behind them. Use logical thinking to connect a claim, a reason and a conclusion. A confident caption is still a claim we can question.
readingBlocks.zh:
档案参访的问题
这张照片能告诉我们什么？
哪些内容需要用其他来源核实？
批判性思维要求检查说法及其背后的证据。运用逻辑思考，把一个主张、理由与结论联系起来。图注即使写得很肯定，仍是一种可以质疑的说法。
readingBlocks.title: Beside the projector

readingBlocks.en:
Lin: I have the skeleton of an essay, but not a complete argument yet.
Tutor: Show me the main points. This is a short assignment, not a dissertation. You don't have to tell the whole history of the town.
Lin: I'd like to acquire a better knowledge of the street first.
Tutor: The acquisition of knowledge takes time. Start with the question on your first page.
readingBlocks.zh:
林：我有了文章提纲，不过论证还不完整。
导师：让我看看主要观点。这是一篇短作业，不是学位论文。你不用讲整个城镇的历史。
林：我想先更好地了解这条街。
导师：知识的获取需要时间。从第一页的问题开始吧。

readingBlocks.en: Lin took a critical look at her own first paragraph. It said the market had always been busy, but one photograph could not show every year. She crossed out always and added the date from the caption. The outline on her desk was small enough to finish. The light on the wall still showed the old bread stall.
readingBlocks.zh: 林审慎地看了看自己的第一段。她写集市一直很忙，可一张照片并不能显示每一年的情况。她划掉“一直”，补上图注里的日期。桌上的提纲终于小到能写完了。墙上的光仍投着那个旧面包摊。

glossary.zh: 装在框中、用于投影的摄影胶片；幻灯片
glossary.note: 本句是带框摄影胶片，slide为单数、slides为复数；用投影仪投射图像。
glossary.example: The lecturer puts a film slide in the projector.
glossary.exampleZh: 讲师把一张胶片幻灯片放进投影仪。

externalEvidence.definition: a transparency mounted in a frame; viewed with a slide projector

glossary.note: draw on + 经验、资料等；不是在照片上画画。
glossary.example: The class can draw on the photographs and written records.
glossary.exampleZh: 课堂可以利用照片与文字记录。

externalEvidence.label: Oxford · draw-on
externalEvidence.findingZh: draw on/upon something利用可用资料或经验；与时间流逝义分开。

glossary.zh: 审慎分析和判断的；批判性的
glossary.note: 指分析与判断，不等于一味责备或表示事态危急。
glossary.example: Lin takes a critical look at her first paragraph.
glossary.exampleZh: 林审慎分析自己的第一段。

externalEvidence.definition: characterized by careful evaluation and judgment

externalEvidence.label: Oxford · critical
externalEvidence.findingZh: 含仔细、公正判断的义项，不只指责错误。

glossary.zh: 审视理由、证据与说法的批判性思维
glossary.note: 整块表示分析评价的思考方式；本例核实论断，而不是刻意挑错。
glossary.example: Critical thinking helps the class examine a confident caption.
glossary.exampleZh: 批判性思维帮助课堂审视一则写得很肯定的图注。

externalEvidence.label: Oxford · critical-thinking
externalEvidence.findingZh: 分析信息并判断可信程度的思维过程。

glossary.zh: 按理由与推理关系思考；逻辑思维
glossary.note: logical thinking用于按理由与推理关系思考，如连接主张、理由和结论。
glossary.example: Logical thinking connects a claim, a reason and a conclusion.
glossary.exampleZh: 逻辑思考把一个主张、理由与结论联系起来。

externalEvidence.definition: thinking that is coherent and logical

glossary.note: 本句为框架的比喻名词；与人体骨架分开。
glossary.example: Lin has the skeleton of an essay.
glossary.exampleZh: 林有了一篇文章的提纲。

externalEvidence.definition: something reduced to its minimal form

glossary.zh: 为获得学位撰写的长篇论文
glossary.note: 长篇学位论文；不用dissertation称普通几页课堂作业。
glossary.example: The short assignment is not a dissertation.
glossary.exampleZh: 这篇短作业不是学位论文。

externalEvidence.definition: a treatise advancing a new point of view resulting from research; usually a requirement for an advanced academic degree

glossary.note: 本句acquire knowledge，获得知识；不是购置地产。
glossary.example: Lin hopes to acquire a better knowledge of the street.
glossary.exampleZh: 林希望对这条街获得更深入的了解。

glossary.note: 不可数过程名词，the acquisition of knowledge；与新收购的物品等义分开。
glossary.example: The acquisition of knowledge takes time.

externalEvidence.definition: the cognitive process of acquiring skill or knowledge

glossary.zh: 支持判断的事实或信息；证据
glossary.note: 本课不可数名词，more evidence，不用an evidence。结果不同是信息，但还不足以确定来源。
glossary.example: The caption needs evidence from another source.
glossary.exampleZh: 图注需要另一个来源的证据。

glossary.note: 本课指学习中被要求完成的一项写作任务。

retrievalPrompts.cue: Explain how the old photographs are shown and how students can use them as a resource.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 说明旧照片怎样显示，以及学生如何把它们当作资源利用。
acceptableAnswers: The lecturer shows framed film slides in a projector. Students can draw on them as well as written records.
checks: 按情境表达，允许其他自然说法

retrievalPrompts.cue: Explain why the caption needs checking and how to connect the argument’s parts.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 说明图注为何需要核实，以及如何把论证部分联系起来。
acceptableAnswers: Take a critical look at the caption. Critical thinking checks its evidence; logical thinking connects the claim, reason and conclusion.
checks: 按情境表达，允许其他自然说法

retrievalPrompts.cue: Tell the tutor what you have written so far and what kind of piece you are working on.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 告诉导师你目前写了什么，以及正在写哪种文章。
acceptableAnswers: I have the skeleton of the assignment. It is a short essay, not a dissertation.
checks: 按情境表达，允许其他自然说法

transferPrompt.cue: You are learning about a new neighbourhood from photos and records. Explain your aim and why it takes time.
transferPrompt.cueZh: 你在通过照片和记录了解一个新街区。说明目标，以及为什么这需要时间。
acceptableAnswers: I want to acquire a better knowledge of the neighbourhood. The acquisition of knowledge takes time, so I will start with one question.
checks: 按情境表达，允许其他自然说法
